issues.title: Select an external IT reader for the comprehension gate
issues.question: Who will read the live English baseline without an introductory call and report what remains unclear?
issues.impact: Internal checks can prove consistency and source coverage but cannot prove that an unfamiliar IT administrator understands Lazurio in ten minutes. The English baseline is live; this test remains the gate for declaring the IT-facing content accepted and will drive any necessary copy revisions.
options: Choose one representative external IT administrator now that the first readable version is live.
Keep audience acceptance open until a suitable reader is available; do not substitute an internal author for the external comprehension test.

issues.title: Align the documentation lockup after the Lazurio logo direction is finalized
issues.question: Which final Lazurio lockup should the documentation header use after the in-progress product identity is approved?
issues.impact: The first release safely uses the text title and the approved favicon. It must not present a working lockup direction as final brand identity.
options: Keep the text title until the design-system owner publishes a final asset.
Adopt the approved asset in a later scoped visual update with browser parity checks.

issues.title: Activate the Organization module slot before Module Setup
issues.question: Will an authorized Organization reviewer approve the exact module registry entry so the documentation slot becomes active?
issues.impact: The repository and content can be prepared, but the canonical lazurio.module.v1 descriptor and Launchpad runtime remain fail-closed while the Organization registry reports planned_slot.
options: Approve and publish the reviewed Organization registry change, update the Organization primary checkout, then run lazurio module setup read-only and with --apply.
Leave the slot planned and keep the documentation repository undeployable from Launchpad. Do not create a hand-written descriptor that bypasses the Organization authority.

issues.title: Confirm availability of advanced GitHub secret-scanning modes
issues.question: Can non-provider pattern scanning and validity checks be enabled for this public repository under the current GitHub Organization plan and policy?
issues.impact: GitHub secret scanning, push protection, vulnerability alerts and Dependabot security updates are enabled. Provider readback still reports the two advanced secret-scanning modes as disabled, so their extra coverage is not currently part of the repository control set.
options: Enable the advanced modes if the Organization plan exposes them and verify provider readback.
Keep standard secret scanning and push protection as the enforced baseline and document the advanced modes as unavailable.

issues.title: Align local Wrangler runtime with the declared compatibility date
issues.question: Which reviewed Wrangler version should replace 4.92.0 so local Pages emulation supports compatibility date 2026-08-26?
issues.impact: Build, CI and Cloudflare deployment work, but local `wrangler pages dev dist` currently fails because its bundled runtime supports dates only through 2026-05-22. Astro development and build artifact checks remain available, but they are not a full Pages runtime smoke.
options: Upgrade the pinned Wrangler version in a separate dependency PR and rerun build plus Pages emulation.
Keep 4.92.0 temporarily and treat CI plus a deployed preview smoke as the provider-runtime proof.

issues.title: Complete post-migration Cloudflare hardening
issues.question: What reviewed sequence should enable DNSSEC and move eligible lazurio.ai hostnames from DNS-only resolution to Cloudflare proxying now that the authoritative cutover has converged?
issues.impact: Cloudflare now owns authoritative DNS and public resolver convergence was verified on 2026-08-26. DNS-only records preserve the previous network path and do not add Cloudflare proxy, WAF or origin shielding to the dashboard or current apex. Enabling proxying before origin TLS and rollback are verified could interrupt service; DNSSEC still requires a separately reviewed, end-to-end activation.
options: Recommended: enable DNSSEC through Cloudflare and WEDOS with end-to-end validation, then proxy the dashboard only after strict origin TLS and a direct-origin protection path are verified.
Keep the dashboard DNS-only until Cloudflare Tunnel or an origin firewall allowlist prevents bypassing the proxy.
Replace the current apex and wildcard only in the separate Lazurio website rollout; do not combine that content cutover with DNS security hardening.
